title: Data Scientist
story: Streamly is a video subscription app with Free, Plus and Pro plans. The product team wants to understand churn and has just run an A/B test on the paywall.

tables.name: users
tables.about: One row per user: plan, channel, age band, city tier, monthly minutes, support tickets, churned (1/0).

tables.name: sessions
tables.about: App sessions: user, date, minutes, main feature used.

tables.name: experiment
tables.about: Paywall test: variant A (control) or B, converted (1/0), revenue.

tasks.title: Churn rate
tasks.question: What percent of users churned? Return one value: churn_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG(churned), 2) AS churn_pct FROM users
tasks.hint: AVG of a 1/0 column is a rate.
tasks.starter:
-- Churn rate
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Users per plan
tasks.question: How many users are on each plan? Return plan and users.
tasks.solution: SELECT plan, COUNT(*) AS users FROM users GROUP BY plan
tasks.hint: GROUP BY plan.
tasks.starter:
-- Users per plan
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Minutes by plan
tasks.question: What are average monthly minutes per plan? Return plan and avg_minutes (2 decimals).
tasks.solution: SELECT plan, ROUND(AVG(monthly_minutes), 2) AS avg_minutes FROM users GROUP BY plan
tasks.hint: AVG and ROUND.
tasks.starter:
-- Minutes by plan
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Churn by channel
tasks.question: Return acquisition_channel, users and churn_pct (2 decimals) for each channel.
tasks.solution: SELECT acquisition_channel, COUNT(*) AS users, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(churned), 2) AS churn_pct FROM users GROUP BY 1
tasks.hint: Same as the overall rate, grouped.
tasks.starter:
-- Churn by channel
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Active days: churned vs retained
tasks.question: Active days = number of distinct dates a user had a session (0 if none). Return churned (1/0) and avg_active_days (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT u.churned, ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(a.days, 0)), 2) AS avg_active_days
FROM users u LEFT JOIN (SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT session_date) AS days FROM sessions GROUP BY 1) a USING (user_id)
GROUP BY u.churned
tasks.hint: LEFT JOIN so users without sessions count as 0.
tasks.starter:
-- Active days: churned vs retained
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Feature mix
tasks.question: What share of sessions used each feature? Return feature and share_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution: SELECT feature, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS share_pct FROM sessions GROUP BY feature
tasks.hint: COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ().
tasks.starter:
-- Feature mix
SELECT *
FROM sessions
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: A/B test readout
tasks.question: Summarise the paywall test: variant, users, conversions, conversion_pct and revenue_per_user (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT variant, COUNT(*) AS users, SUM(converted) AS conversions, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(converted), 2) AS conversion_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(revenue), 2) AS revenue_per_user
FROM experiment GROUP BY variant
tasks.hint: Everything is an aggregate of the experiment table.
tasks.starter:
-- A/B test readout
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Build a feature table
tasks.question: Build one row per user for a churn model: user_id, sessions, total_minutes, active_days and churned. Users without sessions get 0s.
tasks.solution:
SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(s.user_id) AS sessions, COALESCE(SUM(s.minutes), 0) AS total_minutes,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.session_date) AS active_days, u.churned
FROM users u LEFT JOIN sessions s USING (user_id)
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.churned
tasks.hint: LEFT JOIN users to sessions; COUNT(s.user_id) ignores the empty side.
tasks.starter:
-- Build a feature table
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Week-4 retention
tasks.question: For users who signed up in January 2024, what percent had at least one session 21 to 27 days after signup? Return retention_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
WITH c AS (SELECT user_id, signup_date FROM users WHERE signup_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND signup_date < DATE '2024-02-01'),
w AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.user_id FROM c JOIN sessions s USING (user_id)
      WHERE date_diff('day', c.signup_date, s.session_date) BETWEEN 21 AND 27)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM w) / COUNT(*), 2) AS retention_pct FROM c
tasks.hint: date_diff('day', signup_date, session_date) gives days since signup.
tasks.starter:
-- Week-4 retention
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Churn by usage decile
tasks.question: Split users into 10 equal groups by monthly_minutes (NTILE, ordered by monthly_minutes then user_id). Return decile, users, churn_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT decile, COUNT(*) AS users, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(churned), 2) AS churn_pct
FROM (SELECT churned, NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY monthly_minutes, user_id) AS decile FROM users)
GROUP BY decile
tasks.hint: NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY ...) assigns deciles.
tasks.starter:
-- Churn by usage decile
SELECT *
FROM users
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Two-proportion z-test
tasks.question: Compute the pooled two-proportion z statistic for conversion of B vs A: z = (pB - pA) / sqrt(p(1 - p)(1/nA + 1/nB)), p = pooled rate. result: z, 2 decimals.
tasks.solution:
g = experiment.groupby('variant')['converted'].agg(['sum', 'count'])
pa, pb = g.loc['A', 'sum'] / g.loc['A', 'count'], g.loc['B', 'sum'] / g.loc['B', 'count']
p = g['sum'].sum() / g['count'].sum()
se = np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) * (1 / g.loc['A', 'count'] + 1 / g.loc['B', 'count']))
result = round((pb - pa) / se, 2)
tasks.hint: Aggregate conversions and users per variant first.
tasks.starter:
# Two-proportion z-test
# DataFrames ready: users, sessions, experiment
# Put your final answer in a variable called result
result = experiment.head()

tasks.title: Time-based split
tasks.question: Make a time-based split: users who signed up before 2024-05-01 are train, the rest test. result: split, users, churn_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
s = np.where(pd.to_datetime(users['signup_date']) < '2024-05-01', 'train', 'test')
result = users.groupby(s).agg(users=('user_id', 'size'), churn_pct=('churned', 'mean'))
result['churn_pct'] = (result['churn_pct'] * 100).round(2)
result.index.name = 'split'
tasks.hint: np.where builds the split label; group by it.
tasks.starter:
# Time-based split
# DataFrames ready: users, sessions, experiment
# Put your final answer in a variable called result
result = users.head()

tasks.title: Evaluate a baseline
tasks.question: A rule predicts churn = 1 when monthly_minutes < 300. Return accuracy, precision and recall as fractions (2 decimals). result: metric and value, with metric names accuracy, precision, recall.
tasks.solution:
pred = (users['monthly_minutes'] < 300).astype(int)
y = users['churned']
tp = ((pred == 1) & (y == 1)).sum()
result = pd.DataFrame({'metric': ['accuracy', 'precision', 'recall'],
                       'value': [round((pred == y).mean(), 2), round(tp / pred.sum(), 2), round(tp / y.sum(), 2)]})
tasks.hint: precision = TP / predicted positives, recall = TP / actual positives.
tasks.starter:
# Evaluate a baseline
# DataFrames ready: users, sessions, experiment
# Put your final answer in a variable called result
result = users.head()

tasks.title: Which column separates churn most?
tasks.question: For plan, acquisition_channel, age_band and city_tier, compute the spread = highest minus lowest churn rate across its categories, in percentage points. result: column and spread (2 decimals), largest first.
tasks.solution:
rows = []
for c in ['plan', 'acquisition_channel', 'age_band', 'city_tier']:
    r = users.groupby(c)['churned'].mean() * 100
    rows.append((c, round(r.max() - r.min(), 2)))
result = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['column', 'spread']).sort_values('spread', ascending=False)
tasks.hint: Loop over the columns, group by each one.
tasks.starter:
